messages.author: ef27ec9204e3a664
messages.subject: SyntaxError: JSON.parse: bad character in string literal
parts:
Dear all,

I have a rather complex dashboard, that connects to a database and outputs a dropbox with selectible data.

Out of the blue, today the dashboard started crashing.  In the web console the last error is

"SyntaxError: JSON.parse: bad character in string literal"

and then it corresponds to "shiny.js:764"

Other errors I've seen before when the dashboard actually managed to run smoothly.

What does it mean and how do I fix this?

Any help would be greatly, greatly appreciated!

Thank you so much.

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: SyntaxError: JSON.parse: bad character in string literal
parts:
Hi Betty,

Any chance you'd be able open-source the application (either on GitHub or post the code here) or post the application publicly using something like ShinyApps.io or Glimmer/Spark? That would allow us to take a look and see what's going on.

If that's not going to be possible, you'll probably need to look into the messages being sent out from Shiny so you can see which one's causing the problem. Unfortunately, that's a little complicated to do, but if you're using Google Chrome it shouldn't be too painful.

Here's an example of looking at websocket messages in Chrome: http://blog.kaazing.com/2012/05/09/inspecting-websocket-traffic-with-chrome-developer-tools/

If you look at the messages being sent by a Shiny App (example shown below), you can right click any of the messages and click "Copy Message". If you paste the last message sent (probably the one at the top) to us we might be able to identify what's breaking things.

Jeff
